pairs.ownerDecision: 2026-10-27, owner: «Las dos respuestas es lo reocmendado». Estimate, not a measurement: Artificial Analysis has no page for Muse Spark 1.3 below max, so there is no measured figure at low, medium, high or xhigh. They were re-estimated on 2026-10-30 on the scale AA published on 2026-10-29, which rescored every curve and dropped Spark's xhigh. The points follow the shape of the Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 curves, whose low, medium, high and xhigh stand at about 0.49, 0.62, 0.79 and 0.93 of their max; applied to Spark's measured max of 36.4 that gives 17.8, 22.5, 28.7 and 33.9. No minimal row: there is no curve below low to base it on. The slug names no Artificial Analysis page (validation asks only for a non-empty string, as with muse-wonder-full-1.0 reusing another page's slug); it keeps one distinct slug per effort. The cost per task of US$ 0.19 is an estimate too, kept only to rank the pairs and never measured by Artificial Analysis: the median ratio to xhigh of the cost per task at low (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus and Grok: 0.17) applied to Spark's measured xhigh cost of US$ 1.1 gives 0.187, entered rounded to 0.19.

The figures are measured, not estimated: Artificial Analysis gives Muse Wonder at max 52.4 in intelligence, 0.52 in Terminal-Bench 4.0 and a cost per task of US$ 4.54 (its model page, captured 2026-10-26). The models index lists the model among those with no figures only because Artificial Analysis names its family muse-wonder, with no version, and the index matches the family by the model id (muse-wonder-1-0); the owner decision lets the pair in as it does for muse-wonder-full-1.0. Muse takes the effort max for it (model/list of muse serve 1.4.14). Not called for real through the adapter yet.
